question: Who Owns Raising Cane's?
quick_answer: Raising Cane's is owned by its founder, Todd Graves, who started the chain in 1996 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. He remains the majority owner and co-CEO, and the company is privately held, so it does not trade on a stock exchange. The brand is named after Graves's dog, Raising Cane.
key_facts: Founder and majority owner: Todd Graves
Known for serving only chicken finger meals

body.heading: Who owns Raising Cane's?
body.text: Raising Cane's is owned by Todd Graves, who founded it and is still the majority owner and co-CEO. The company has stayed privately held rather than going public, so there is no Raising Cane's stock to buy. Graves's large ownership stake has made him one of the wealthiest restaurant founders in the US.

body.heading: How it started
body.text: Graves opened the first Raising Cane's in 1996 near the Louisiana State University campus in Baton Rouge. The idea came from a college business plan built around one focused product: quality chicken finger meals. The restaurant is named after his dog, Raising Cane.

body.heading: Still founder-led
body.text: Unlike many big chains that sold to investment firms, Raising Cane's has remained founder-led. Graves continues to shape the brand, and keeping it private has let the company grow on its own terms while sticking to its simple, chicken-only menu.

faqs.a: No. Raising Cane's is privately held and owned mainly by founder Todd Graves, so you cannot buy shares in it.
